messages:
zoe (ml-infra): Quick share — finished a 6h latency/throughput sweep for the A100-80 across three clouds. Varying driver + CUDA + MIG on/off. Posting the condensed results and a few oddities we should follow up on.

sam (bench): Nice. paste the summary pls.

zoe (ml-infra): Summary table (batch=1 baseline, seq=1024, prompt caching disabled):
```
region    | driver    | cuda  | mig  | p50(ms) | p99(ms) | qps
aws-usw2  | 525.105   | 12.1  | off  | 18      | 120     | 320
gcp-usc1  | 525.105   | 12.1  | off  | 20      | 150     | 300
azure-wus2| 510.60    | 11.8  | off  | 30      | 400     | 220
aws-usw2  | 525.105   | 12.1  | on   | 22      | 140     | 280
gcp-usc1  | 525.105   | 12.1  | on   | 24      | 170     | 260
azure-wus2| 510.60    | 11.8  | on   | 35      | 520     | 180
```
Notes: p99 numbers are token-level tail (end-to-end inference). All runs used same model binary and quantization disabled.

mira (models): Whoa azure p99 is huge. Any SIGSEGVs or kernel errors in logs?

zoe (ml-infra): No crashes. We see a lot of kernel fallback lines in dmesg and `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows different PCI topology on azure instances. Also clock governor not in performance mode by default on that SKU.

devon (runtime): That matches a local repro — on 510.x driver we hit a fallback to emulation kernels for our fused attention path. Upgrading to 525 fixed the kernel selection on GCP and AWS. Azure's image seems to ship 510 by default even for the same SKU.

sam (bench): Did you try rebuilding with `--cuda-arch=sm_80` and pinning kernel flags?

zoe (ml-infra): I built a quick kernel shim and retested on azure with driver forced to 525. Results improved but still ~20% worse p99 than AWS with same driver. Suspect BIOS power/clock ceilings + PCIe gen differences.

bench-bot: Raw CSV + perf traces uploaded: s3://redwood-sweeps/1829001123/a100-multi-region-sweep.tar.gz

mira (models): Any quality diffs from quant runs? We should run quantized fp16->int8 sweep too, to check regression sensitivity at tail.

zoe (ml-infra): Good call. I did a small int8 sweep (post-training quant) on GCP vs Azure — latency improved but p99 deltas stayed similar; quality (perplexity) unchanged. So tail isn't model-quality, it's infra/kernel.

devon (runtime): Action items I propose:
- repro on a clean Azure image with driver 525 and CUDA 12.1 (already partially done)
- snapshot `dmesg` + `nvprof` traces and compare kernel names
- test CPU governor set to performance and lock GPU clocks via nvidia-smi
- try MIG scheduler tweaks (we saw slight qps stability impact when MIG is on)

sam (bench): Also run a batch=4 and bs=8 workload to see batching mask impact on tail. Sometimes small batches hide kernel latency.

zoe (ml-infra): Agreed. I'll run the governor + clock lock + 525 image sweep tonight in westus2 and post delta.

deploy-bot: Heads-up: if we pin 525 in our autoscale images, some older dedicated nodes will need revalidation for compatibility with older customer rollouts. Opened infra ticket INF-734.

mira (models): If azure still lags after all infra fixes, we should add a routing policy to prefer GCP/AWS for latency-critical customers in that region.

zoe (ml-infra): Filing issue: ML-1829 with all traces + steps. Will tag @devon @sam @mira. Thanks — will report back tomorrow with updated numbers. :thumbsup:
